answer: The best time to renovate a restaurant or bar is your own slowest stretch, and that depends on the venue: patios often peak from late spring to early fall, event spaces around the holidays and wedding months. Put heavy work in your slow weeks, quicker work after close or on closed days, and line up approvals early.

blocks.x: In hospitality, the space is part of the product. A tired bar top, worn floors or a cramped layout shows up in reviews and in how long guests stay. But every day closed is a day without revenue, so knowing when to renovate a restaurant or bar matters as much as the design of any hospitality renovation in Winnipeg, MB.
Know your calendar: when to renovate a restaurant or bar
Winnipeg hospitality businesses have very different peaks:
**Patios and summer venues** are often busiest from late spring to early fall.
**Event and banquet spaces** often peak around the holiday season and wedding months.
**Cafés and lunch spots** follow office and school schedules.
**Venues near arenas and festival sites** follow event calendars.
Plan heavy work for your slowest weeks, and book your contractor well in advance so you get those dates.
High-impact hospitality upgrades
**Bar and service areas.** A new bar top, back bar, lighting and better workflow behind the bar can improve service speed and guest experience.
**Seating and layout.** Reconfiguring seating can add covers, create private areas for groups, or improve flow from entrance to bar to washrooms.
**Lighting and acoustics.** Warm, layered lighting and sound-absorbing finishes can change the mood of a room, and can often be phased.
**Washrooms.** Guests notice. Updated fixtures, finishes and lighting signal that the whole business is cared for.
**Flooring.** Durable, slip-resistant flooring stands up to boots, salt and spills through a Winnipeg winter.
**Entrances and patios.** A welcoming entry, good signage and a refreshed patio can extend your season and your street presence.

blocks.x: Loud work has limits. Within 150 metres of a home, the [City's hours](https://www.winnipeg.ca/building-development/property-records/construction-your-neighbourhood) for it run from 7 a.m. on weekdays and 9 a.m. on weekends and holidays, and end at 9 p.m. every day. How long each closure runs depends on your scope, so ask for a written schedule built backwards from your reopening date.
Permits and approvals

Many hospitality renovations in Winnipeg need City of Winnipeg building, plumbing or electrical permits. Changes to occupancy loads, exits, washrooms or kitchens may also involve fire or public health approvals, and [floor plans for a food premises go for public health review](https://gov.mb.ca/health/publichealth/environmentalhealth/protection/food.html) before any construction or renovation. In an older building, have suspect materials [tested for asbestos](/blog/asbestos-testing-before-renovating-manitoba) before demolition.

Serving alcohol takes a liquor service licence from the Liquor, Gaming and Cannabis Authority of Manitoba, and [licensees must notify the authority of major renovations](https://lgcamb.ca/liquor/liquor-service-licences-2/how-to-apply/). Confirm requirements early so approvals don't delay reopening. Our [restaurant renovation checklist](/blog/restaurant-renovation-checklist-winnipeg) sets out the steps by stage.
Questions to ask your contractor
How will you phase the work so we can keep serving?
Can you work after close or on closed days?
How will you protect food and bar areas from dust?
What's your plan if something unexpected delays reopening?
The bottom line
The best hospitality renovations are planned around the calendar: big work in slow weeks, quick wins after hours, and approvals lined up early.
